Alright, gang, it's Saturday, November 7, 2026. The world's still spinning, Trump's still tweeting, and your boy's got the lowdown on everything that matters (and a few things that probably don't, but are still kinda fun). Grab your overpriced coffee, let's dive in.

---

**Money Talk**

- **Healthcare stocks get the jitters with new Dem Congress.**
  Looks like the blue wave that swept DC has healthcare investors clutching their pearls. With Democrats taking control, expect policy shifts that could put a damper on their party. [S1]
- **Berkshire Hathaway doubles down on buybacks as profits dip.**
  Warren Buffett's crew is feeling the pinch from lower operating and overall profits, but they're still playing the long game. They more than doubled share repurchases in Q3. Classic, understated confidence, or a warning shot? You decide. [S2]
- **AI is sparking a small business boom, no employees needed.**
  Forget "Help Wanted" signs – America's newest small business owners are leveraging AI for finance, marketing, and design, essentially replacing the need for a human workforce. Talk about lean and mean. [S3]
- **Renewable energy catches a tailwind post-midterms.**
  The conservative war on clean energy hit a major roadblock with Trump and the GOP's midterm trouncing. Investors, take note: green is the new gold, at least in Washington. [S4]
- **AI stocks roller coaster after midterm results.**
  First, they tanked on fears of Democratic regulation, then they climbed back up. Apparently, investors had a moment of clarity and decided slower AI development isn't *quite* as bad as they initially thought. Or maybe they just remembered AI's still gonna eat the world. [S8][S9]
- **UK homeowners feel the squeeze as mortgages jump.**
  Brace yourselves, UK friends. Rising interest rates mean many are seeing their monthly mortgage payments go up by a cool £200. That's a lot of avocado toast you're not having. [S6]

**World Lore**

- **Paraguayan President ousted, under house arrest.**
  Talk about a bad Friday. President Santiago Peña was impeached and placed under house arrest after a state-affiliated bank collapsed. Apparently, the Senate had had enough. [S21]
- **VP Vance pushes for new Iran deal in secret talks.**
  Vice President Vance is skipping the public theatrics and going full "back channel" with Iran, trying to hash out a ceasefire and restart nuclear negotiations. High stakes, low profile. [S17]
- **Europe hit with another wave of flight and broadcaster bomb threats.**
  Just when you thought it was safe to fly, more bomb threats are causing diversions and disrupting European airspace and media. It's either a very bad prankster or a highly coordinated nuisance campaign. [S25]
- **Pope Leo XIV kicks off South America tour post-cancer surgery.**
  The pontiff, fresh off lung cancer surgery, is on a 12-day, three-country tour through Uruguay, Argentina, and Peru. He's already celebrated Mass for over 40,000 in Uruguay. Clearly, you can't keep a good Pope down. [S23][S31]
- **Trump swaps out Chief of Staff for Stephen Miller.**
  In a move that signals zero chill, President Trump, still reeling from midterm losses, replaced his chief of staff Susie Wiles with the famously maximalist Stephen Miller. Expect "limitless presidential power" to be the new White House mantra. [S16][S18]

**Tech Tea**

- **Binance CFO bails after massive $6.3 billion hack.**
  The crypto exchange is having a rough week. Hot on the heels of a colossal $6.3 billion hack, their CFO is jetting off to "pursue a new venture." Coincidence? Probably not. [S41]
- **Apple Keyboard has a secret "blacklist" of un-swipable phrases.**
  Ever struggled to swipe "male chauvinist pig" on your iPhone? Turns out, Apple's keyboard has a hidden blacklist of phrases it just won't help you with. Free speech, or helpful filter? The line gets blurrier every day. [S36]
- **Musk hints at ditching Cybertruck for autonomous "Cybercabs."**
  Just when you thought Tesla's electric truck couldn't get weirder, Elon Musk suggests he's winding down Cybertruck production to make way for Cybercabs – driverless autonomous taxis. Never a dull moment in the Musk-verse. [S7]
- **US approved Nvidia chip sales to an empty office in China.**
  You'd think vetting tech exports would be, you know, thorough. But apparently, the Commerce Department and Nvidia let crucial H200 AI chips go to a Chinese firm whose offices were literally empty. "New Matrix" indeed. [S50]
- **Fridge-hacking spree is an IoT wake-up call.**
  If you thought your smart fridge was just chilling, think again. Escalating hacks on internet-connected devices, from blood labs to grocery stores, are showing the very real risks to critical infrastructure from basic security lapses. Lock down your smart devices, people. [S51]

**Creator Szn**

- **Instagram eyes long-form content, but creators are hesitant.**
  Instagram is trying to lure long-form video creators away from YouTube, but the creators themselves are side-eyeing the move, questioning whether the platform can offer enough exposure to make it worth their while. Fair point. [S57]
- **Amazon's shopping agent now serves text orders, with ads.**
  Get ready for more sponsored content, this time in your DMs. Amazon's new AI shopping agent takes orders via text, and those reply threads will be prime real estate for Sponsored Product ads. Your thumbs, their revenue. [S56]
- **Holiday marketing still belongs to celebrities, not creators.**
  Despite riding the creator wave all year, marketers are reverting to tradition for the holiday crunch. When it comes to the festive season, it seems the big bucks still go to Hollywood A-listers, not your favorite TikToker. [S59]
- **Ad tech landscape shows a widening divide.**
  While some players like AppLovin are surging, others are struggling as CTV growth masks the ongoing pains in the open-web ad market. It's a tale of two ad tech cities, and creators caught in the middle will feel it. [S58]

**Supply Lines**

- **Zipline's valuation soars with expanded Walmart drone deal.**
  Drone delivery startup Zipline is absolutely crushing it, with a rocketing valuation and a beefed-up partnership with Walmart. Clearly, those autonomous sky-delivery ambitions are paying off big. [S86]
- **Amazon Prime members get free Uber Eats delivery.**
  Amazon is making moves in the last-mile battle, giving Prime members $0 delivery fees on Uber Eats. This is a direct shot across the bow at DoorDash and signals Amazon's relentless push into every corner of your life. [S82][S84][S85]
- **DHL Group reports strong Q3 revenue, raises annual outlook.**
  Good news for the yellow and red. DHL announced an increase in revenue for the third quarter of 2026 and is raising its annual search outlook. Strong performance, despite what IAG Cargo's woes might suggest about air freight generally. [S79]
- **Freight fraud: compromised communications behind 40% of stolen loads.**
  It's not just sophisticated hacks; a new report shows a striking 40% of direct theft incidents are linked to compromised communications. Plus, fraudulent calls are up 90%. Talk about a security headache for the trucking world. [S62]
- **Aurora's autonomous truck production hits a snag.**
  The self-driving truck company Aurora is facing delays in its production schedule due to supply and quality issues. They're still aiming for over 1,000 trucks by the end of 2027, but the road to autonomy is rarely smooth. [S67]
- **Container spot rates calm, but Middle East tensions still loom.**
  The ocean freight market is enjoying a brief moment of tranquility with slight declines in transpacific and Asia-Europe rates as capacity eased. However, the 'fragile' Middle East situation remains a major threat, reminding everyone that peace on the seas is never guaranteed. [S71]

**Speed Round**

- Berkshire Hathaway is doubling down on buybacks even as profits take a hit.
- Pope Leo XIV, fresh from cancer surgery, is on a 3-country South America tour.
- Apple's keyboard has a literal blacklist of phrases your iPhone won't help you swipe.
- Marketers are still choosing celebrities over creators for the crucial holiday ad season.
- A new study links 'safe' plastic food packaging chemicals to lower birth weight. Yikes.
- The US let Nvidia sell AI chips to an *empty office* in China. Oversight, anyone?
- UK homeowners are seeing mortgage payments jump by £200 a month thanks to rising rates.
